arguments.prompt:
Read the problem statement at /input_artifacts/problem.md and derive the canonical 131-character P/N classification string for pile sizes 0 through 130.

Your task:
1. Read the problem statement to understand the game rules
2. Enumerate the legal move set as the union of perfect squares up to 130 (1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100, 121) and triangular numbers up to 130 (1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28, 36, 45, 55, 66, 78, 91, 105, 120), removing duplicates
3. Set up the recurrence: dp[0] = P (base case), and for k from 1 to 130: dp[k] = N if there exists a legal move m ≤ k such that dp[k-m] = P, otherwise dp[k] = P
4. Compute the full 131-character classification string for positions 0 through 130
5. List the P-position indices (where the string has 'P')

Return a JSON object with:
- "legal_move_set": the sorted list of distinct legal moves
- "classification_string": the 131-character P/N string
- "p_positions": list of indices where the classification is P

Do NOT read any candidate responses. Only solve the canonical problem.

Read the task instruction carefully and produce a code-boundary guide for applying the eight failure-reason codes.

The eight failure-reason codes are:
1. wrong_base_case - triggered when classification at pile size 0 is N instead of P, or when response states empty pile can still move or wins
2. missing_subtraction_moves - triggered when response enumerates incomplete move set (omits squares or triangulars, or specific values)
3. pn_convention_swapped - triggered when response uses opposite P/N convention (P=current player wins) or final string matches bitwise inverse of correct classification
4. wrong_loss_convention - triggered when response treats misère convention (last player to move loses) or inconsistent base case
5. truncated_or_short_string - triggered when final classification string is not exactly 131 characters from {P,N}
6. arbitrary_pattern_heuristic - triggered when classification rests on unjustified pattern (all even are P, every fifth is P) without computing game tree
7. arithmetic_recursion_error - triggered when correct recurrence is set up but final string has per-position computation mistakes (string length is 131, convention correct)
8. non_terminating_or_no_final_string - triggered when no identifiable 131-character P/N string is produced (loops, mid-truncation, refusal)

Produce a disambiguation guide that clarifies:
- Codes are evaluated as exact sets per response - both extra and missing codes are wrong
- Each code applies only when triggering condition is concretely instantiated in response text
- Precedence rules for overlapping triggers
- What textual evidence is required for each code
- When to use arithmetic_recursion_error vs arbitrary_pattern_heuristic
- When to use truncated_or_short_string vs non_terminating_or_no_final_string
- When missing_subtraction_moves applies (requires concrete incomplete enumeration, not silence)

Return your guide as a structured text document.
